## reference · planned-maintenance-percentage
* Planned maintenance percentage (PMP) measures the number of planned maintenance tasks compared to all maintenance tasks.
* PMP is expressed as the percentage of total maintenance hours spent on planned maintenance tasks in a given period.
* PMP = # of planned maintenance hours ÷ # of total maintenance hours × 100
* Organizations with best-in-class maintenance have a PMP of 85% or higher.
* Top performing organizations complete about 30% usage-based maintenance, 50% condition-based maintenance, and 5% run to failure maintenance.
* Planned maintenance can help reduce downtime by up to 18%.
* Measuring PMP allows maintenance teams to gain insight into time efficiency, downtime reduction, compliance with safety regulations, and cost effectiveness.
* A higher PMP means an increase in planned tasks, allowing for better scheduling of labour and parts, and reducing instances of over-scheduling and over-purchasing.
* PMP can be used to control costs through resource efficiency and downtime reduction.
Sources: https://www.fiixsoftware.com/maintenance-metrics/planned-maintenance-percentage/
